# .NET Blazor Apps & Games — Global Audit Prompt

Use this prompt when you are ready to crawl all `.NET` / Blazor apps and games under `C:\Users\punko\Downloads\_CODEMATT` and populate `GLOBAL/blazor_apps/`:

```text
Act as an expert .NET/Blazor Solution Architect, Game Developer, and Frontend Engineer.

Analyze all my sub-folders under C:\Users\punko\Downloads\_CODEMATT and find my .NET Blazor apps and games (identifying Blazor Server/WebAssembly, .razor components, C# game loops, and UI files). Create a comprehensive, single-file HTML report at GLOBAL/blazor_apps/blazor_overview.html (plus a reusable crawler/builder in GLOBAL/blazor_apps/scripts/ and a time-based tracker in GLOBAL/blazor_apps/history/blazor_progress_over_time.html) broken down into 3 levels:

LEVEL 1: ARCHITECTURE & HIGH-LEVEL GRID (Overview)
- Global master grid comparing all Blazor projects: Project Name, Hosting Model (Server/WASM), Primary Type (Utility, Game, Dashboard), Interactive Mode (Server, WebAssembly, Auto, Static), Key NuGet Dependencies, and Active State.
- Visual KPIs: Total App Count, Hosting Model Breakdown, Game vs. Line-of-Business ratio, Total Components Mapped.

LEVEL 2: UI, STATE, & GAME FLOW (The "What" & Component Diagrams)
- Expandable detail view for each project:
  - Component Hierarchy Diagram (visual SVG/CSS tree of MainLayout -> Pages -> Components -> GameLoop)
  - Page & Route Inventory (`@page "/..."`)
  - State Management & Services (DI Services, cascading parameters, local storage, game state)
  - Game Loops & Canvas Details (update/render cycle, tick rate, inputs, rendering tech)

LEVEL 3: TECHNICAL DETAILS & PERFORMANCE (Specs & Code)
- File/LOC breakdown (C# vs. Razor vs. JS interop)
- Component communication types (EventCallbacks, Services, JSInterop)
- Dependency Injection matrix (Scoped, Transient, Singleton)
- Performance & Optimization (WASM AOT, prerendering, lifecycle methods)
- Key Files to inspect (clickable relative links)

OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS:
- Single offline-ready HTML file matching the dark theme of GLOBAL/index.html, with interactive search/filtering, sorting, and collapsible sections.
- Include a one-click updater (GLOBAL/blazor_apps/update_blazor.bat) and link GLOBAL/index.html to blazor_apps/blazor_overview.html and blazor_apps/history/blazor_progress_over_time.html.
```

documents.title: Unity ↔ Unreal Agent Transfer & Parity Checklist
documents.markdown:
# Unity ↔ Unreal Agent Transfer & Parity Checklist

Use this checklist whenever moving a trained `.onnx` policy or MJCF body between a **Unity 6 (`org.mujoco` + Sentis)** project and an **Unreal 5.8 (URLab + NNE ORT)** project.

## 1. Pre-Transfer Compatibility Check
- [ ] Run the socket dry-run check:
  ```powershell
  python GLOBAL\rl_training\standards\vault_import.py "<SourceRepo>/path/to/policy.onnx" <TargetRepo> --dry-run
  ```
- [ ] Confirm both repos use **MuJoCo** physics (ML-Agents / Unity PhysX brains cannot drop into MuJoCo directly).
- [ ] Confirm the ONNX **opset is 17** (or verified supported by both Unity Sentis and Unreal NNE ORT).

## 2. Body (MJCF) Parity
- [ ] Copy the source character's MJCF `.xml` (and referenced meshes) into the target repo if the target does not already have the exact same body.
- [ ] Verify **joint count**, **actuator order**, **control ranges (`ctrlrange`)**, and **PD gains (`kp` / `kv`)** match between training XML and target engine XML.
- [ ] Verify simulation timestep & control rate match (**50 Hz** policy step: e.g. `dt = 0.002 × 10` or `dt = 0.005 × 4`).

## 3. Observation & Action Parity
- [ ] Compare the source observation builder (Python/C#/C++) against the target engine's observation builder feature-by-feature:
  - Gravity vector / root orientation convention (quaternion `w,x,y,z` vs `x,y,z,w`).
  - Angular/linear velocity frame (world frame vs. root-local frame).
  - Joint position offsets (raw `qpos` vs. `qpos - default_qpos`).
  - Phase/gait clock or command vector slots.
- [ ] Verify action post-processing matches: `target_q = default_q + action_scale * clip(action, -1, 1)` (or baked inside ONNX).

## 4. Runtime Smoke Test
- [ ] Feed a fixed zero/test observation vector into Python `onnxruntime` and into the target engine (Sentis / NNE) and confirm max output diff `< 1e-4`.
- [ ] Run a 10-second stand/idle test in the target engine scene with zero commands — verify no exploding joints, NaNs, or instant falls.
- [ ] If the observation layout differs slightly, either add a thin observation adapter in the target controller or use the imported `.onnx` as a **teacher policy** to distill/warm-start in the target repo.

documents.title: Cross-Platform RL Training Standards (Unity ↔ Unreal)
documents.markdown:
# Cross-Platform RL Training Standards (Unity ↔ Unreal)

This folder defines the **shared contract** that allows trained `.onnx` agents and MuJoCo bodies to move between **Unity 6 (`org.mujoco` + Sentis)** and **Unreal 5.8 (URLab + NNE ORT)** projects in `_CODEMATT`.

## Why agents can move across engines
Every MuJoCo-based project in the fleet simulates the **same physics engine (MuJoCo)** and executes **standard `.onnx` policy graphs**. Engine differences (Unity left-handed Y-up vs. Unreal left-handed Z-up) live purely in the renderer/bridge layer — as long as both sides follow the same **4-part contract**, a brain trained for one engine runs in the other without retraining physics from scratch.

---

## The 4-Part Portability Contract

### 1. Body & Physics (MJCF)
- **Single source of truth:** Every portable character is defined by a self-contained **MJCF `.xml`** file (joints, actuators, masses, collision geoms, PD gains).
- **Joint order is immutable:** The order of `<actuator>` entries in the MJCF defines the action vector indices `0..N-1`. Never reorder actuators between projects without remapping.
- **Control rate:** Target **50 Hz policy control** (`dt = 0.002` with 10 substeps, or `dt = 0.005` with 4 substeps).
- **Physics engine boundary:** MuJoCo brains (`PoOlympic`, `PoHillKing`, `PoBox`, `PoBasketball`, `PoSlapUnreal`, `PoRaceUnreal`, `PoRobotTrain`) share physics. Unity PhysX / ML-Agents repos (`PoFootball`, `PoSoccer`, `PoSumo`) do not share MuJoCo bodies.

### 2. Socket (`obs → action`)
A brain's **socket** is its `(observation_dim → action_dim)` shape plus the exact ordering/units of every observation feature.
- See [`sockets.json`](sockets.json) for the catalog of active sockets across the fleet.
- **Cross-engine shared socket today:** `103 → 29` (29-DoF G1-family humanoid, used by both **PoHillKing [Unity]** and **PoRaceUnreal [Unreal]**).
- **Target standard for new humanoids:** Use the **29-DoF G1-family** MJCF and standardize the base proprioception prefix (root height/orientation/vel, joint pos/vel, previous action) before appending game-specific task senses.

### 3. ONNX Export Contract (Unity Sentis ↔ Unreal NNE ORT)
- **Opset:** Export at **ONNX opset 17** (supported cleanly by both Unity Sentis and Unreal NNE ORT across all current repos).
- **Tensor names & shapes:**
  - Input: `obs` with shape `[1, obs_dim]` (or `['batch', obs_dim]`), `float32`, no NaNs.
  - Output: `actions` (or `action` / `ctrl`) with shape `[1, act_dim]`, `float32`, deterministic policy mean (strip exploration noise and optional critic heads if the target runtime expects a single output).
- **Normalization baked in:** Bake observation running-mean/std normalization and action clipping/scaling into the exported ONNX graph whenever possible, so Unity and Unreal do not have to duplicate stats files.

### 4. Parity Verification
Before declaring a brain portable across engines, run the checks in [`parity_checklist.md`](parity_checklist.md):
1. Same MJCF body & timestep.
2. Same observation vector values (within `1e-4`) on an identical pose/frame.
3. Same ONNX output tensor on a fixed dummy observation vector in Python ORT, Unity Sentis, and Unreal NNE.
4. Stand/idle smoke test in the target engine for 10 seconds without divergence.

---

## Tools in This Folder

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`sockets.json`](sockets.json) | Machine-readable catalog of fleet sockets, opsets, tensor names, and body families. |
| [`parity_checklist.md`](parity_checklist.md) | Step-by-step Unity ↔ Unreal transfer & parity verification checklist. |
| [`vault_import.py`](vault_import.py) | Safely copy an `.onnx` brain into another repo (`vault_imports/<SourceRepo>/`), check socket compatibility (`FITS` vs `ADAPTER NEEDED`), and write a `.vault.json` provenance sidecar. |
| [`quick_transfer_actions.py`](quick_transfer_actions.py) | Curated cross-game transfer recipes & 0–2 h quick training actions rendered in the RL Dashboard. |

### Safe Brain Import Command
Run from `_CODEMATT`:
```powershell
python GLOBAL\rl_training\standards\vault_import.py "<SourceRepo>/path/to/brain.onnx" <TargetRepo> --dry-run
```
Drop `--dry-run` to copy the brain into `<TargetRepo>/vault_imports/<SourceRepo>/` without overwriting existing files.

documents.markdown:
# RL Training Simulations (MuJoCo & ML-Agents) — Global Audit Prompt

Use this prompt whenever you want to expand, re-audit, or add new RL repositories to `GLOBAL/rl_training/`:

```text
Act as an expert AI/RL Scientist, Robotics Engineer (MuJoCo), and Game AI Dev (ML-Agents).

Analyze all RL repositories under the workspace root that contains this `GLOBAL/` directory (Unreal 5.8 + URLab + MuJoCo Warp + NNE ORT, Unity 6 + org.mujoco + MuJoCo Warp + Sentis, and Unity 6 + ML-Agents PPO/MA-POCA). Update the scripts in GLOBAL/rl_training/scripts/ and regenerate:
1. GLOBAL/rl_training/rl_training_overview.html
   - Level 1: Master comparison matrix, global KPIs, speed & complexity charts
   - Plain-English & Portability section (10 non-technical views: 10x10 portability matrix, human-practice-per-hour speed chart, character passports, skill library, coaching styles, 4-point plug-and-play checklist, gym graduation ladder, pocket brains vs specialist teams, gym-to-game 3-stack pipeline, and top starter recipes)
   - Level 2: Per-repo behaviors, senses/actions, reward & penalty matrices, SVG episode flow diagrams, and real embedded GIFs/screenshots
   - Level 3: Physics/skeleton specs, hyperparameters, parity gates, and direct links to source files
2. GLOBAL/rl_training/history/rl_progress_over_time.html
   - Append a new timestamped snapshot to GLOBAL/rl_training/history/timeline.jsonl and snapshots/
   - Plot brains/behaviors learned over time, benchmark speed improvements, run-over-run deltas, and recently trained .onnx files
```

## Quick Refresh (No Prompt Needed)
Double-click `GLOBAL\rl_training\update_rl.bat` or run:
```powershell
.\GLOBAL\rl_training\update_rl.bat --open
```
